evidence: Read the brief and all three notes cold, and checked them against the workbook wording ('casual/terse is good; not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated') and quality-checks.md:15 defects (uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, voice shift between instruction.md and notes). (1) Sounds like a real requester with reasons: instruction.md:1 'our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last'; instruction.md:3 'so old chat doesn't pile up ... what has gone must stay gone'; conversations.md:5 'Our clients ask several things at once, so answers have to stay with their question'; conversations.md:9 'People fix typos and figures'; conversations.md:13 'Clients paste all sorts into chat'; conversations.md:29 'Our internet in court is patchy.'; walls-and-retention.md:17 'because a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us'; walls-and-retention.md:19 'Conflicts come up mid-matter'; integration.md:7 'which is why we care that the order stays consistent.' (2) Sentence variety and terse lines: short sentences next to long ones, e.g. 'Two things matter more than anything else.' (instruction.md:3), 'Dev Anand is walled from M-12 today.' (walls-and-retention.md:15), 'Only a partner changes a timer.' (walls-and-retention.md:23). Contractions throughout (doesn't, mustn't, can't, isn't, don't, won't, I'm, I've). (3) No gloss: grep for seamless|robust|delve|ensure|leverage|utiliz|comprehensive|intuitive|shall and em dashes in all four files returned nothing; 'must' appears only in ordinary speech (instruction.md:3, conversations.md:29,31). No bullet lists anywhere; the only table is the account roster (walls-and-retention.md:5-11), which is data, not parallel prose bullets. (4) Voice is consistent: instruction.md and all notes speak as the firm in first person plural ('we/our/us'); conversations.md:25 and :31 switch to 'I' when talking about the individual's own unread line and half-typed reply, which a real staff member naturally does ('Each of us has our own unread count ... When I open a matter') and is not a register change. Minor observations, not defects for this row: a few declarative paragraphs are denser and more spec-like (walls-and-retention.md:35 transcript contents; walls-and-retention.md:37 'When something you try is refused, the reason appears next to what you did and stays until you change it.'; integration.md:3 'not necessarily from inside /app, so find your own files relative to server.js'). They are still plain first-person firm prose with no robotic cadence; whether they read as an acceptance checklist is row 1's question, not voice. Adversarial check: a less natural alternative (numbered MUST list, 'seamless, robust' marketing copy, or a brief in casual voice with notes in formal spec voice) would fail this row; the shipped text has none of those. A broken or conforming app is irrelevant to a prose-voice row, so no app counterexample applies. Runtime evidence is not required for this row; the template files contain only CHANGE_ME placeholders, so all voice text is task-authored and editable.
